reason: All named characters in this text occupy positions of significant authority, power, or religious importance. The named individuals include: kings (Hezekiah, Sennacherib, Tirhakah, Esarhaddon, David), high-ranking officials (Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, Joah the recorder), Assyrian commanders (Tartan, Rab-saris, Rab-shakeh), royal princes (Adrammelech, Sharezer), and the prophet Isaiah. Even parenthetical mentions like Hilkiah and Asaph (identified only as fathers of officials) are from prominent families. No ordinary, common citizens are named or given individual agency in this narrative—only rulers, officials, military commanders, and prophets appear by name.
